text:
Meera: heads-up — seeing steady memory growth on qwen-2.7 runs with long contexts (~32k tokens). kv cache size keeps climbing even after identical prompt repeats.
Matt: oh interesting — is it leak or fragmentation?
Meera: looks like fragmentation + reuse miss. profiler shows pages allocated but free-list not reusable for same key ids. attaching minimal trace: 
```
kv_cache_pages: 1024 -> 1476
kv_free_pages: 210
kv_reuse_hits: 18
fragmentation_pct: 38.4
long_seq_allocs: +14MB/min
```
Liam: do we see this across MQA/GQA variants or specific to Qwen?
Meera: mostly Qwen-2.7 (MQA build). I ran a quick compare: llama-2.2 MQA shows lower fragmentation, mistral v1.1 GQA seems fine too. Qwen's stride/rope scaling seems to cause different cache layout patterns.
Anika: can you paste the reproduce command? I can spin a headless job.
Meera: sure: 
```
curl -X POST https://local-redwood/serve/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"model":"qwen-2.7-mqa","input":"<long-context-repeat-1k>","max_tokens":1024}'
```
run that in a loop with different segment alignments (shift prompt by 64, 128 tokens).
Matt: I suspect page binning is keyed by seq_len mod 64 or something. if rope scaling modifies INTERNAL_CACHE_KEY (layer,head,seq_mod) we could end up with many unique cache keys instead of reusing.
Meera: exactly. profiler shows per-layer key variance spikes at layers 12-16 where rope frequency changes. also observed more small allocations (sub-page) which increases fragmentation.
Liam: any correlation with kernel selection? maybe certain kernels produce different kv layouts (packed vs interleaved)
Meera: yes — when runtime picks the "packed-kv" kernel for MQA we get contiguous allocations, reuse good. but for the "strided-kv" kernel (used when rope scaling mismatch detected) we allocate per-head small buffers.
Anika: do we have a quick mitigation? e.g., force packed kernel or coalesce free-list entries?
Meera: forcing packed kernel reduces fragmentation by ~60% in my local runs, but latency goes up ~4-7% for short contexts. tradeoff. also a patch to normalize rope phase in cache key (ignore scaling offset) reduces unique keys by ~70% and keeps reuse high.
Matt: hmm that patch might change semantics if different rope phases produce different attention outputs. need to ensure numerical equivalence or only normalize for cache-keying while keeping computation unchanged.
Meera: plan: 1) run A/B: packed-kernel forced vs patch-normalize-key on staging for 24h w/ synthetic traffic; 2) add metric kv_key_uniques_per_min; 3) add a GC pass that coalesces small free pages every N seconds as fallback.
Liam: can infra-bot schedule the canary?
infra-bot: scheduled canary: service=runtime-qwen, variant=packed-kernel, start=2026-03-18T02:00:00Z, duration=24h, notify=@eng-runtime.
Anika: thanks. one more ask — add a short perf test that runs long-context chat and measures memory-growth per-token. I can add to perf harness.
Meera: added task in the thread: re-run profiler with traces after canary and post results. if normalization passes numerics, we'll make it default for Qwen MQA.
Matt: +1. also open a follow-up to inspect allocator fragmentation heuristics — maybe grow page size for small-buffer patterns.
Meera: yep. I'll open PRs: (1) key-normalize (2) packed-kernel toggle (3) allocator-coalesce. posting links when ready. :thumbsup:
